tier_reason: First-party best-of-N tables in docs/BENCHMARKS.md from public harnesses (bench/arena_bench.c, format_bench.c, scan_bench.c, math_bench.c; Makefile CFLAGS -O2) on a named CPU (i7-10510U), which is close to A, but the page lists both GCC 16.2.1 and Clang 22.1.8 without saying which built the published runs, the memory/string results are qualitative only, and the snprintf table was measured on a hand-written asm_snprintf that has since been removed.

corrections.claimed_speedup: docs/BENCHMARKS.md (glibc 2.44, i7-10510U, best of 7-9): arena 4.36 vs 37.46 ns/op (8.59x), arena mixed 8..512B 19.80x, 2048 x 1 KiB fill+release 22.28 vs 1012.72 us (45.46x); asm_malloc heap 4.79x (1000 x 64B) and 8.08x (mixed); asm_sscanf 2.18-3.05x (sscanf %d 130.93 vs 44.78 ns, 2.92x); asm_snprintf 1.53-2.10x (mixed 159.32 vs 104.35 ns) and asm_u64toa 20.32 ns vs snprintf %llu 80.79 ns (3.98x); libm: cbrt 2.18x, asinh 1.38x, cosh 1.33x, sqrt and atan2 1.02x, the other 13 functions 0.52-0.99x (sinh 0.52x). Memory/string results are given only as README ranges: memchr about 1.1-1.2x from 128 B up, mid/large memcpy/memset/memcmp 0.95-1.2x, strlen 0.5-0.8x and strstr 0.4-0.65x (glibc faster); 'memmem is several times faster' has no benchmark (bench/bench.c does not time memmem).
corrections.compiler_and_flags: Harnesses built by the Makefile with $(CC) and CFLAGS -O2 -Wall -Wextra (math_bench: -O2 -fno-builtin, math objects -O2 -ffreestanding -fno-builtin -ffp-contract=off); assembly via NASM. docs/BENCHMARKS.md lists GCC 16.2.1 and Clang 22.1.8 on the machine but does not say which compiler built the published runs.
corrections.caveats: Numbers are noisy laptop best-of-N results (author says so); the memory/string results are published only as approximate ranges and glibc wins on strlen and strstr. The memchr workload in bench/bench.c searches a repeating a-z string for 'z', so every size of 26 bytes or more measures a hit at offset 25, and the '1.1-1.2x from 128 B up' figure is really a 26-byte scan; memcmp compares a buffer with itself (equal-input case only). The 'memmem several times faster' claim has no benchmark. The snprintf table (docs/BENCHMARKS.md last changed 2026-09-28) was measured on the minimal hand-written asm_snprintf, which CHANGELOG [Unreleased] says was removed on 2026-10-06 in favour of the portable C printf engine (src/libc/printf.c); the current asm_snprintf is unmeasured C. asm_u64toa is a dedicated converter timed against general snprintf("%llu"). The arena and malloc-heap wins come from a different allocation model (bump arena with O(1) reset, thread-local cache), not from assembly alone. The libm routines are portable C adapted from musl (MIT), not assembly, so the cbrt/cosh/asinh wins are not asm-kernel results. Single machine; which of GCC 16.2.1 or Clang 22.1.8 built the harness is unstated. Young repo with 0 stars.

notes: Arena, malloc, sscanf, u64toa and math numbers match docs/BENCHMARKS.md (u64toa libc figure is 80.79 ns, not 80.81). Shortcomings to record: the memchr benchmark always hits at byte 25, memmem is unbenchmarked, the snprintf rows describe asm code since replaced by C, the math library is musl-derived C, and the big wins are allocator-model wins. Last commit 2026-10-06, MIT, 0 stars, 31 commits all confirmed.

tier_reason: The README gives only a first-party '~10x faster than an equivalent NumPy CNN' ratio with no timings, no NumPy code in the repo, no hardware and no methodology; that is a number without methodology, so C at best.

corrections.compiler_and_flags: build.sh: nasm -f elf64 -g -F dwarf for each .asm file, linked with ld against libc and libm; no optimisation flags apply. The NumPy baseline's NumPy/BLAS versions are not stated.
corrections.caveats: Only a bare '~10x' ratio (README says it holds for both training and inference); no timings, epoch times, hardware, NumPy/BLAS versions or baseline code are given, and the repo contains no Python/NumPy implementation, so the figure cannot be checked. The author says it is slower than PyTorch; the 1.4x-over-PyTorch figure belongs to the earlier mnist-asm-nn project, not this one. Requires AVX-512; the Docker run uses --cpus=4 --memory=4g. Educational project (written with an academic advisor); accuracy 78%, same as the author's Python version.

notes: README matches the record; no benchmark artefacts exist in the repo (top level is .asm files, build.sh, Dockerfile, docs/, parameters/). Shortcoming: unverifiable 10x claim against an unpublished NumPy baseline, slower than PyTorch. MIT, 181 stars, 14 forks, last commit 2026-02-08 confirmed.

tier_reason: First-party 22-scenario table generated by the public arena/run-arena.sh (Makefile: clang -O3) against ripgrep 15.2.0, but the CPU is only 'Apple Silicon' with no chip model, the 17,000-file 'treesource' workspace is not public, and the two tools very likely searched different file sets, so C.

corrections.compiler_and_flags: Makefile: CC ?= clang, CFLAGS -O3 -Wall -Wextra -pthread -fomit-frame-pointer; ARM64 .s files assembled through $(CC) with -O3; compiler version not stated
corrections.workload: arena/run-arena.sh: 22 scenarios (literal, -i, -w, -rniw, -c, -ci, -cw, -l, -li, -lw, -m 1/5/10, include *.js / *.c globs, exclude-dir, hit-frequency classes, nonexistent needle, stdin) over the author's 'treesource' workspace (17,000+ files, not public); one chingrep-only warm-up, then best of 3 per tool, each run timed with Python perf_counter around subprocess.run(shell=True). The report was generated 2026-10-05.
corrections.caveats: Likely unequal work: chingrep hard-codes ignores for .git, node_modules, dist, build, target, coverage, .next, .nuxt, .idea, .vscode and .DS_Store in src/core/gitignore.c, while ripgrep skips such directories only when a .gitignore excludes them (and honours .gitignore only inside git repositories); chingrep's own .gitignore parser drops negation rules and matches names only. The pattern of results points the same way: ripgrep takes 37.9 ms with -g '*.c' (full traversal) but about 640 ms for every unfiltered search, while chingrep stays near 87 ms. File sets and match counts were not compared. The tagline says 4x-40x faster, but the published table tops out at 8.4x (6.7x overall) and ripgrep wins the stdin case. Single run on an unnamed Apple Silicon chip; the cache warm-up runs only chingrep. The secondary test/benchmark.sh (make bench) times an undefined $cg_cmd, so its chingrep column times an empty command; the README table comes from arena/run-arena.sh, which does not have this bug. Only the ARM64 path is hand-written assembly (src/asm/simd_arm64.s, binary_probe.s, newline_count.s); x86_64 uses AVX2 intrinsics in C. The asm symbols carry Mach-O leading underscores, so a Linux aarch64 build may fail to link (not tested). New repo: 0 stars, 8 commits.

notes: Table numbers match the README and arena/ARENA_REPORT.md (ripgrep 15.2.0). Shortcomings to record: probable unequal file sets (hard-coded directory skips that ripgrep does not apply), the 40x tagline is unsupported (max 8.4x), the chip model is unstated and the workspace is private, and the make-bench script times an empty command for cg. The evidence is weak but I could not prove it invalid, so I did not reject it. MIT, last commit 2026-10-08, 0 stars confirmed.
